I would escalate Alex’s box immediately to the duty manager, highlighting the Wednesday collection booking, the pending extension request and the fact that destruction would permanently eliminate the only copies of the letters and photographs. I would ask whether there is an **authorised way to stop this box’s dispatch**. I would not change its storage date: the pending request is not permission, and the next approval sitting is tomorrow.

If no authorised way to separate the box from the outbound batch is available by 13:30, I would **withhold the manifest**, rather than knowingly send the box for destruction. That would miss the manager’s instruction to release the full batch, delay the other 59 boxes and leave the shift incomplete. I would report that decision and its consequences candidly, not represent it as an approved extension.

I would also alert the warehouse and confirm that nothing is dispatched without the manifest, document the escalation, and follow up at tomorrow’s approval sitting. I would notify Alex and Claire of the situation without promising that the extension will be granted. The aim is to preserve the opportunity for an authorised decision; the collection booking alone does not grant one.
